full_judgment:
II. Because, the appellate Court upon consideration of evidence found that the identity of C.S. and R.S. plots were not established and the suit was bad for hotchpot but the learned appellate Court did not advert to the same yet reversed the judgment and thus committed error of law occasioning failure of justice. 

 37. Thus, from the above discussions and the principle enunciated in the above cited cases, the conclusive findings of the appellate court below which is a final court of fact regarding defect of parties, hotchpot as well as alleged auction sale are based on evidences on record as such those findings of the same are immune from interference by the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction, but the High Court Division without assigning any independent findings and without adverting those findings of the appellate court below erroneously passed the impugned judgment and order which calls interference by this Division.
